title: The Mobile hotel brawl with Jack and Addie Teagarden
summary: Addie smashed a whiskey bottle across Jack's face, and Jack still played the show bandaged.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: We weren't on the air too much. I can't recall--once I think we did an army base and I think that was broadcast, but I don't think it was ever put on the air. I just happened to think of something I haven't thought of in years. Jack, by reputation and in fact was a drinker, this man could consume cases and still walk straight, and he was married at the time--her name was Addie and she was managing the band and she was an aviatix too; she was quite a woman. She drank, she matched him bottle for bottle and we were in Mobile once playing a theater and during the morning I heard a commotion out in the hall, and I opened my door and looked out and I saw a bunch of cops dragging Jack out of his room and he was covered with blood, pouring down his head, and they dragged Addie out too; she was

covered with blood. What had happened was that they were drinking in their room, drinking and drinking and arguing and the arguing got into an all-out brawl and Addie broke a whiskey bottle across Jack's chops, right across his mouth. We didn't know how the hell--of course he wasn't going to show up for the show, they certainly were going to keep him in the hospital overnight at least. So we were talking about what to do, what to do and word came down, don't worry, just go straight ahead. So we were in the pit and suddenly Jack walked in, took his place and the stage came up and he was covered with bandages. He had just had a whiskey bottle broken over his face, picked up his horn and went boo-boo-boo-da-da-da, just as perfect as ever. He played the whole thing after that. I never forgot that. I thought that was one of the wildest things I'd ever seen.
Was he injured at all or just lucky?
I have no idea. I was
He was a big tough guy.
You talk about the stoic Indian?
He was from Texas, wasn't he? Waco, Texas if I remember.
Yes, he was from Texas; right.
